html:
The We Wai Kai, also known as the Cape Mudge First Nation, are a branch of the Laich-kwil-tach, the southernmost Kwakwaka'wakw people, based on Quadra Island off Campbell River, British Columbia.

In the 1800s the Laich-kwil-tach moved south and took over land at the north end of the Strait of Georgia from Coast Salish peoples such as the K'ómoks. Their close kin are the We Wai Kum across the water at Campbell River.

After Canada banned the potlatch, police seized masks and regalia at a great potlatch at Village Island in 1921. Some of these were returned in the 1970s and are kept at the Nuyumbalees Cultural Centre at Cape Mudge.
sum: The We Wai Kai, also known as the Cape Mudge First Nation, are a branch of the Laich-kwil-tach, the southernmost Kwakwaka'wakw people, based on Quadra Island off Campbell River, British Columbia.
